'''Ulla Mitzdorf''' (15 March 1944&nbsp;– 19 July 2013) was a German scientist. She contributed to diverse areas including [[physics]], [[chemistry]], [[psychology]], [[physiology]], [[medicine]] and [[gender studies]].

==Life and Scientific Work==
Mitzdorf gained her doctorate in [[theoretical chemistry]] in 1974 at the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref name="Nökert_2017">{{cite web |title=Ulla Mitzdorf német tudós (1944–2013) |url=https://nokert.hu/p-20170331-2147/1784/8/ulla-mitzdorf-nemet-tudos-1944-2013 |website=Nőkért.hu |access-date=24 February 2024 |language=hu-HU |date=31 March 2017}}</ref> Subsequently, she worked as a scholar at the [[Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry|Max-Planck Institute of Psychiatry]] in [[Munich]]. In 1983, she habilitated in physiology,<ref name="Chronik_lmu_1986_1988">{{cite book |title=Chronik der Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München 1986–1988 |publisher=Präsidialkollegium der Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München |location=Munich |isbn=3-922480-05-5 |page=29 |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/12174087.pdf |access-date=6 April 2021}}</ref> and in 1984 in [[medical psychology]] and [[Neuroscience|neurobiology]] at [[LMU Munich]].

From 1988 to 2009, she was the Fiebiger Professor for medical psychology at LMU Munich.<ref name="Chronik_lmu_1986_1988"/> Simultaneously, from 2000 to 2006, she was women's affairs officer and spokeswoman for the state conference of women and gender equality officers in Bavarian universities.

Ulla Mitzdorf significantly contributed to the understanding of [[local field potentials]] (LFPs) in the [[central nervous system]]. By implementing the technique of current source density (CSD),<ref name="LFP_Analysis">{{cite book |last1=Destexhe |first1=Alain |last2=Goldberg |first2=Joshua A. |chapter=LFP Analysis: Overview |title=Encyclopedia of Computational Neuroscience |date=2014 |pages=1–5 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-7320-6_782-1|isbn=978-1-4614-7320-6 }}</ref> she provided additional evidence for the theory that cortical LFPs result from the synaptic activity<ref name="LFP_Analysis"/> in the brain.

Mitzdorf died after a short illness on 19 July 2013, aged 69.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ehemalige LMU-Frauenbeauftragte verstorben - Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München |url=https://www.uni-muenchen.de/aktuelles/news/2013/mitzdorf.html |website=www.uni-muenchen.de |access-date=22 November 2020 |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407111704/https://www.uni-muenchen.de/aktuelles/news/2013/mitzdorf.html |archive-date = 7 April 2020}}</ref>
